title: Online Prediction of Stochastic Sequences with High Probability Regret Bounds
claim: Average regret per round decays toward zero as sequence length grows, with the spread across runs narrowing over time.
layout: single panel, left-to-right, nested shaded quantile bands around a red mean line
description: A single line-and-band plot. The x-axis is sequence length, from 0 to 300. The y-axis is average regret per round, from 0 to about 0.22. A thick red curve for the mean starts near 0.21 and falls steeply, then flattens to about 0.03 at length 300. Around it are nested blue shaded bands. They run from the darkest 40–60% quantile band to the palest min-to-max band, and the legend at upper right labels each one. The bands are wide at short sequence lengths and narrow as length grows. Their edges have small sawtooth jumps. The eye goes first to the red mean curve and the dark blue core, then to the widening pale tails that show the heavy upper tail of regret.
caption: Average regret per round for a Markov chain with memory order $\memory=3$ and $\numStates=2$ states. Shown are the mean and selected quantiles for $4,000$ runs.
abstract: We revisit the classical problem of universal prediction of stochastic sequences with a finite time horizon $T$ known to the learner. The question we investigate is whether it is possible to derive vanishing regret bounds that hold with high probability, complementing existing bounds from the literature that hold in expectation. We propose such high-probability bounds which have a very similar form as the prior expectation bounds. For the case of universal prediction of a stochastic process over a countable alphabet, our bound states a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2} Î´^{-1/2})$ with probability as least $1-Î´$ compared to prior known in-expectation bounds of the order $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$. We also propose an impossibility result which proves that it is not possible to improve the exponent of $Î´$ in a bound of the same form without making additional assumptions.
